name: Diclofenac
executiveSummary: Phenylacetic NSAID with analgesic, antipyretic, and anti-inflammatory effects. Usual adult dose 75–150 mg/day; pediatric oral 0.5–2 mg/kg/day (up to 3 mg/kg/day in JIA) per label.
indications:
## Indications

- Acute musculoskeletal pain and inflammation (postoperative, traumatic, rheumatologic).
- Dysmenorrhea and colic.
- Juvenile idiopathic / rheumatoid arthritis under specialist care.

## Precautions and contraindications

- Avoid in active peptic ulcer, GI bleeding, severe renal/hepatic failure, decompensated heart failure, third trimester of pregnancy, and NSAID/ASA allergy.
- Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.
- IM/IV not routinely recommended in children (limited pediatric safety/efficacy on many labels); prefer oral/rectal when authorized.

> Calculate pediatrics by **weight**. Confirm salt (sodium/potassium) and strength before dosing.

adulto.presentation: Tablets 25–50–75 mg (immediate or modified release); ampoules 75 mg/3 mL; topical gel by brand.
adulto.dose: Pain/inflammation PO: **75–150 mg/day** in 2–3 doses (e.g. 50 mg every 8–12 h). Dysmenorrhea: start 50–100 mg, then 50 mg every 8 h; usual max **150 mg/day** (some labels allow 200 mg on day 1 only). IV/IM: 75 mg every 12 h; max 150 mg/day; short course (usually ≤ 2 days IV/IM).
adulto.administration: PO with food if gastric intolerance. IV: dilute per label and infuse slowly (e.g. 30 min–2 h). Deep IM.
adulto.notes: Do not combine with other NSAIDs. GI, renal, and CV risk; check anticoagulants, antiplatelets, lithium, methotrexate, and ACEI/ARB.

pediatrico.presentation: Oral suspension (e.g. 1.8–2 mg/mL diclofenac); tablets; ampoules 75 mg/3 mL (restricted use).
pediatrico.dose: PO ≥ 1 year: **0.5–2 mg/kg/day** in 2–3 doses. JIA: up to **3 mg/kg/day** in divided doses under specialist care. **Daily maximum: 150 mg/day**. > 12–14 years: near-adult regimens (e.g. 50 mg every 8–12 h), usually not exceeding 150 mg/day. IV/IM: not routine < 14–18 years; if used under protocol, adult ceiling 150 mg/day and shortest duration.
pediatrico.administration: Prefer PO. IV: dilute to ~1 mg/mL in 0.9% NaCl or 5% dextrose; infuse 30 min–2 h with pump. Deep IM only if indicated.
pediatrico.notes: Many EU labels discourage adult-strength tablets/suppositories under 14 years. Check local product minimum age (ANMAT).

neonatal.presentation: No routine oral/IV diclofenac regimen for neonatal fever/pain.
neonatal.dose: Do not use in neonates unless exceptional indication and explicit institutional protocol.
neonatal.notes: Disproportionate renal and GI risk; not part of standard neonatal antipyretic care.

stability:
## Stability / storage

- Opened ampoule: discard remainder; do not save for later doses.
- Suspension: shake; store per label.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Dyspepsia, abdominal pain, nausea, diarrhea; dizziness, headache, rash; elevated transaminases. Serious: peptic ulcer/GI bleeding, AKI, thrombotic CV events, hypersensitivity/bronchospasm.
